confirm.text: These are multi-select entries on the air job / OWL forms, not confirmed events. Per Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance, technicians may select "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose. They are listed here for the technician to confirm.
"Stop work authority utilized" was not selected on any form today. That is the item that indicates authority was actually exercised, and it appears nowhere in the day's 47 air job forms.
Seven forms selected only the routine pre-job item "Stop work authority was discussed", with no unsafe-conditions selection. These are not stop-work events and need no follow-up:
1099 Gage Gonzales — XBC Giddings Estate 1404H — 35140_2
Alexander Clubb — Bend A #1 — 35148_1
Andrew Bailey — Frances 12-1-A #2801H — 35158_1
Andrew Bailey — Glaspie Havard 11Q 17H — 35121_1
Dawson Drake — University 10-11C 3H — 35139_1
Michael Jobe — Northeast Scharbauer 1219H — 35134_1 (also selected "Unsafe conditions", see below)
Michael Jobe — Elkin Crawford 34EE 105H — 35132 (also selected "Unsafe conditions", see below)
Three forms selected "Unsafe conditions" and need the technician's confirmation:

Michael Jobe — Northeast Scharbauer 1219H — 03:03 PM — 35134_1. This one is supported by a narrative that names an actual condition: "One of the crew didn't have Ppe on so I told him to get his stuff on". That reads as a real observation, corrected on the spot, involving a customer crew member rather than a Canon technician. Worth confirming whether it was raised with the company man.

Michael Jobe — Elkin Crawford 34EE 105H — 10:33 AM — 35132. "Unsafe conditions" selected, but the supporting narrative reads only "Had a meeting went over everything that needed to be done for job" and the close-out is otherwise positive. No unsafe condition is described anywhere on the form.

1099 Ruben Rojo — XBC Giddings Estate 4201H — 03:00 PM — 35119_1. "Unsafe conditions" selected with no stop-work item. The only narrative is "Reconnect", and the entire Learn close-out is blank, so there is no positive narrative to offset the selection.

Repeat pattern: Michael Jobe selected "Unsafe conditions" with no supporting narrative twice in one day on 09/26 and has now done so again on 35132. That is the same defect two reporting periods running and is worth raising with him directly as a training point rather than as an incident. Ruben Rojo appeared on this list on 09/23 under similar circumstances (blank close-out). Nathan Contreras and Jose Campos, both previously on this list, selected neither stop-work item on any of today's forms.

The inverse is also present, and matters more. Alexander Clubb's two forms both describe real conditions without the corresponding selection. On Bend A #1 he recorded a burst 2-inch line and an hour-long work stoppage but selected only "Stop work authority was discussed" and not "Unsafe conditions". On Hooper 39 #1 he recorded "Wellhead was leaking slowly." and selected neither. This is the same gap seen with Jordan Lemmons on 09/26 — the narrative is the reliable record and the multi-select is not tracking it.

Carried-forward selections: the identical eight-item string beginning "Job scope completed safely and as planned,Safety control measures were utilized..." appears verbatim on at least nine forms today across six different technicians. That suggests the selection is being carried forward rather than made fresh each job, which is the underlying training point.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. In particular, fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images and not as extractable text, so this review cannot confirm any of them. The FR uniform figure, the hydro and cascade entries, the stop-work selections and the narrative fields are all text and were read directly.

84 of 84 submissions read. Both job boards were available — the 9/29 ArkLaTex and Permian Basin boards emailed by Blake Walton at 10:03 AM Central were used. 75 manned rows were checked across the two boards, of which 62 were live assignments after removing cancelled, unassigned, WTX support, shop and days-off rows. The search window closes at midnight Central and this review ran at 11:00 PM, so any submission landing in the final hour of the day, or arriving late tomorrow morning for today's work, is not included and would need to be picked up in tomorrow's review.
